Read a DHS data file directly

Source: R/read.R
bdhs_read_file.Rd

Reads a Stata (.dta), SPSS (.sav) or SAS (.sas7bdat) DHS file, or a DHS zip archive containing one, without importing it, using the same conventions as bdhs_read(): lower-case names, labels kept, column selection without reading the whole file. The survey round and recode are identified with bdhs_identify_file() and stored as attributes.

Usage

bdhs_read_file(
  path,
  vars = NULL,
  vars_regex = NULL,
  indicators = NULL,
  keep_design = TRUE,
  labels = c("haven", "factor", "codes"),
  n_max = Inf
)

Arguments

path

Path to the file.

vars

Variables to read (case-insensitive). NULL reads all of them unless vars_regex is given. Requested variables that do not exist in the file are skipped with a warning.

vars_regex

Regular expressions; variables whose (lower-case) names match any of them are read too.

indicators

Indicator ids from bdhs_indicator_list(). Every variable these indicators need is read, so the result can go straight into bdhs_estimate(). Combines with vars and vars_regex.

keep_design

If TRUE (default) and variables are selected, also read the identifiers, survey design variables and interview dates needed to link files, detect the round and build a survey design with bdhs_design(): caseid, hhid, hvidx, bidx, midx, v000-v003, v005, v007, v008, v021-v025 (and their hv/mv equivalents), the child's birth date and age (b3, b19) and the all-woman factors awfact*.

labels

How to return labelled variables: "haven" (default) keeps haven::labelled() columns; "factor" converts every variable whose values are all labelled to a factor with haven::as_factor() (levels = "labels"), leaving partially labelled variables such as z-scores with flag codes as labelled numbers; "codes" drops value labels (keeping variable labels) and turns extended missing values into plain NA.

n_max

Maximum number of rows to read.

Value

A tibble with the attributes bdhs_survey_id, bdhs_recode and bdhs_file when the file could be identified.

See also

Other data store: bdhs_data_dir(), bdhs_download(), bdhs_forget(), bdhs_identify_file(), bdhs_import(), bdhs_inventory(), bdhs_read(), bdhs_sitrep()

Examples

f <- file.path(tempdir(), "BDHS2022KR.dta")
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR", n_clusters = 4, households = 3), f)
kr <- bdhs_read_file(f, vars = c("hw70", "b4"))
attr(kr, "bdhs_survey_id")
#> [1] "BD2022DHS"
